text:
Maria: Heads-up — seeing a steady upwards shift in token-level latency for /v1/generate on dedicated-pool-3 since ~03:10UTC. p99 went from ~420ms -> 680ms over the last 45m.
Kevin: saw that. spikes line up with a bunch of medium-length requests (~512 tokens) coming in. profiler shows kernel fallback on some attention ops.
Sylvia: can you paste the profiler snippet? My guess is a kernel-selection regression where we fail to pick the quantized fast kernel for that seq length.
Kevin: paste below — from runtime-profiler @ 03:18
```
[03:18:22] kernel_selector: model=a1-ggml v=2.1.3 selected_kernel=generic_gemm reason="no optimized kernel for seq=512,bs=1"
[03:18:22] kvcache: hit_ratio=0.72, misses=129, evictions=3
[03:18:22] batcher: avg_batch_size=2.1, max_latency_us=1200000
```
Maria: kvcache hit ratio drop is interesting — before the spike it was ~0.92. If prefix distribution changed we might be re-hashing leading to more cold-start KV loads.
Nate: I checked the per-route KPIs on the dedicated dashboard — route /v1/generate on pool-3 shows kv_miss_count spike aligned with two tenants that had a burst of varied prompts.
Lee: sounds like two things: 1) kernel selector falling back to slower path for certain seq lengths, 2) KV cache churn from mixed-prefix workload causing batching to be less efficient.
Sylvia: agree. suggestions: (A) add kernel-selection telemetry to dashboards (rate of fallbacks + per-kernel average tokens/s), (B) split kv cache hit ratio by prefix hash bucket and tenant, (C) show effective batch size distribution by route and pool.
Kevin: drafted some query snippets for Grafana panels (Datadog-style metrics names here for clarity):
```
# kernel fallback rate
sum:runtime.kernel_selection{pool:dedi-pool-3,model:a1-ggml,selection=fallback}.as_rate() by {seq_len}

# kv cache hit ratio per-prefix
avg:kvcache.hits{pool:dedi-pool-3} / (avg:kvcache.hits{pool:dedi-pool-3} + avg:kvcache.misses{pool:dedi-pool-3}) by {prefix_bucket}

# token-level latency p99 by route+pool
p99:runtime.token_latency_ms{route:v1_generate, pool:dedi-pool-3} by {route,pool}

# effective batch size histogram
histogram:batcher.effective_batch_size{pool:dedi-pool-3,route:v1_generate}
```
Maria: perfect. Also want a per-pool headroom panel: free_gpu_mem_gb, queued_requests, active_tasks per GPU. we need a single-number headroom heuristic: headroom = free_gpu_mem_gb / avg_mem_per_task.
Nate: added a noisy-neighbor detector prototype: if (active_tasks_per_gpu variance across GPUs in pool) > 0.35 && p95(token_latency) increased by >20% for >5m -> noisy-neighbor alert. Results: pool-3 crossed threshold at 03:14.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-042 (noisy neighbor alert for dedi-pool-3). Owner: @Kevin
Lee: can we also instrument kernel selection latency (how long selector takes)? we've seen selection overheads sometimes in extreme churn leading to micro-latency.
Sylvia: good call. add metric runtime.kernel_selection_duration_ms and a small histogram. Then can correlate selection_duration p99 with token latency p99.
Kevin: quick repro on staging: I ran a mixed-prefix workload hitting seq sizes 256, 384, 512, with random prompt prefixes and saw fallback rate jump ~12% for seq=512 when model build used kernel-db v2.1.3. rolling back kernel-db -> v2.1.2 drops fallback to 0.9%.
Maria: that indicates we introduced a kernel-regression in 2.1.3. need a rollback plan if this impacts customers. but first, dashboards + alerts so we catch earlier.
Nate: proposed dashboard panels to add to "Dedicated Pools / pool-3 / Performance":
- Token latency breakdown (p50/p90/p95/p99) by route
- Kernel selection: fallback_rate, avg_tokens_per_kernel, selection_duration_ms
- KV cache: hit_ratio_by_prefix_bucket, miss_latency_ms, evictions
- Batcher: avg_batch_size, batch_wait_time_ms, effective_batch_efficiency (tokens_saved/expected)
- Pool headroom: free_gpu_mem_gb, avg_mem_per_task, headroom_score, active_tasks_per_gpu_variance
- Noisy neighbor alarm status + recent offenders (tenant id list)
Kevin: alert thresholds (draft):
- token_latency_p99(route) > baseline * 1.5 for 5m -> P2 notify #eng-runtime + #oncall
- kernel_fallback_rate > 5% for 10m -> P3 notify runtime owners
- kvcache_hit_ratio < 0.8 for 3m -> P3 paging to infra oncall
- active_tasks_per_gpu_variance > 0.35 and p95_token_latency increase >20% for 5m -> P1 noisy-neighbor paging
Maria: assign owners: Kevin -> kernel selector rollback/patch, Sylvia -> dashboard + kernel_selection_duration telemetry, Nate -> noisy-neighbor detection tuning + tenant attribution, Lee -> kv cache instrumentation.
Sylvia: I'll spin up a Grafana branch and add panels, and a prebuilt dashboard JSON. Will post PR link when ready.
Maria: For the immediate mitigation — can we add a routing rule to fall back to pool-2 for /v1/generate where latency is stable? That reduces impact while we fix.
Kevin: yes, can add a temporary smart-route: prefer pools with kernel_fallback_rate < 1% for seq distribution matching request. I'll put a short-term policy in place.
infra-bot: Change request created: CR-20260318-17 (smart-routing policy for v1_generate). Owner: @Kevin
Lee: will also look at whether kv cache partitioning by tenant would help reduce churn. early thought: per-tenant prefix sharding + small LRU window per tenant.
Nate: action items summary:
1) Sylvia: add kernel_selection_duration_ms + panels (ETA 2h)
2) Lee: kv cache per-prefix bucket telemetry + panel (ETA 4h)
3) Kevin: temporary routing policy + rollback plan for kernel-db (ETA 1h)
4) Nate: refine noisy-neighbor detector thresholds and tenant attribution (ETA 2h)
5) Maria: coordinate customer comms if rollback required (oncall)
Maria: Thanks all — let's keep updates here. If anyone sees p99 > 700ms again, ping oncall immediately.
Kevin: noted. I'll post the PRs and the rollback playbook link once ready.
